sourceNote.title: Invoice PDF export
sourceNote.html:
Invoice PDF export

Testing the Export PDF action on the invoice detail page of a demo accounting app.

  • Invoice states: draft, sent, paid, cancelled. Only sent and paid invoices can be exported; draft and cancelled show the button disabled with a tooltip.

  • The PDF contains company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate (0%, 9%, 21%) and totals.

  • Invoices with more than 25 line items continue on a second page with the header repeated.

  • File name is invoice-<number>.pdf.

  • Observed: an invoice with a customer name containing "Müller & Söhne" exported fine, but the ampersand looked escaped in the file name preview.

  • Observed: export of a 60-line invoice took about 8 seconds with no progress indicator.

bodyHtml:
Scenario: Export availability by invoice state

Risk notes: Prioritize state restrictions because they determine which invoices can be exported. Likelihood and recent change history were not supplied.

Test case: Export sent and paid invoices

Purpose: Verify export is available for both eligible states.

Preconditions: Sent and paid invoices are available in the demo accounting app.

Test data: One sent invoice and one paid invoice.

Steps:

  • Open each invoice’s detail page.

  • Select Export PDF for each invoice and inspect the exported file.

Expected result: Export PDF is enabled and produces a PDF for both states.

Coverage notes: Covers both permitted invoice states.

Test case: Prevent export of draft and cancelled invoices

Purpose: Verify export restrictions and their explanation.

Preconditions: Draft and cancelled invoices are available.

Test data: One draft invoice and one cancelled invoice.

Steps:

  • Open each invoice’s detail page and inspect Export PDF.

  • Hover over the disabled button to inspect its tooltip.

Expected result: Export PDF is disabled and a tooltip is shown for both states.

Coverage notes: Negative coverage for both prohibited states. Tooltip wording is not specified.

Scenario: PDF content accuracy

Risk notes: Missing or incorrect invoice content could compromise the exported document’s usefulness.

Test case: Preserve invoice details, VAT rates and totals

Purpose: Verify the PDF contains the required invoice information.

Preconditions: A sent or paid invoice is available with a company logo and line items covering the stated VAT rates.

Test data: Invoice containing VAT rates of 0%, 9% and 21%.

Steps:

  • Export the invoice from its detail page.

  • Compare the PDF’s company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate and totals against the invoice.

Expected result: All listed content is present and matches the invoice.

Coverage notes: Covers all three stated VAT rates. Calculation and rounding rules were not supplied.

Scenario: Pagination and large exports

Risk notes: The page threshold creates a boundary risk. The observed 60-line export also warrants checking completion and recording waiting behavior.

Test case: Check the 25-line boundary and 60-line export

Purpose: Verify pagination, repeated headers and successful export of a larger invoice.

Preconditions: Exportable invoices with the required line counts are available.

Test data: Invoices with 25, 26 and 60 line items.

Steps:

  • Export each invoice; record the elapsed time and any progress indication for the 60-line invoice.

  • Inspect pagination and confirm all line items are retained.

  • Inspect the second-page header for invoices exceeding 25 line items.

Expected result: All exports complete with all line items present. Invoices with more than 25 line items continue onto a second page with the header repeated.

Coverage notes: Covers the threshold and the first value above it. The note does not explicitly define the page count for exactly 25 items. Preserved observation: a 60-line export took about 8 seconds with no progress indicator; no timing limit or progress-indicator requirement was supplied.

Scenario: Filename and special-character handling

Risk notes: The observed escaped ampersand makes filename preview handling a targeted regression area.

Test case: Export an invoice for Müller & Söhne

Purpose: Verify successful export and the prescribed filename while checking the observed preview behavior.

Preconditions: A sent or paid invoice for Müller & Söhne is available with a known invoice number.

Test data: Customer name: Müller & Söhne; the selected invoice’s number.

Steps:

  • Open the invoice detail page and select Export PDF.

  • Inspect the filename preview and record how the ampersand appears.

  • Inspect the exported filename and open the PDF.

Expected result: Export succeeds, the PDF opens, and its filename follows invoice-[number].pdf using the invoice number.

Coverage notes: Preserved observation: this customer name exported successfully, but the ampersand looked escaped in the filename preview. Preview formatting requirements were not supplied.
